title: The Billable Hour Is Cracking: The Margin Question Every IT and Management Consultancy Now Faces
linkedin:
A consultant we spoke with recently finished a scoping report in under half a day. Eighteen months ago the same report took two and a half days. She billed the same day rate as always, and felt slightly odd about it.

That feeling is becoming common across IT and management consulting firms. AI tools are now doing the first draft, the data pull, the code scaffold. The work still gets reviewed and delivered by a human, but the raw hours behind it are shrinking. Salaries, leases and software costs are not shrinking with them.

Here is the part worth sitting with: utilisation can look perfectly healthy on paper, hours charged against hours available, while realisation, the rate those hours actually convert into collected revenue at the intended price, quietly slips underneath it. Revenue holds steady even as delivery gets faster, because the fee model hasn't caught up with how quickly the work now moves.

Clients were never really paying for hours. They were paying for a solved problem. Firms that reprice around scope and outcome, rather than time logged, tend to hold their margin through this shift. The ones still billing by the clock are the ones who will feel this first.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog. Link in the first comment.

A quick note for owners of IT consultancies, management consulting practices and similar professional services firms across Brisbane, Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria. AI tools are genuinely speeding up the work, first drafts, data analysis, scoping documents, code scaffolding. That is a good thing for clients and for turnaround times.

What it also does, quietly, is shrink the hours behind each engagement while overheads such as salaries, leases and software stay exactly the same. For firms still billing by the hour, that mismatch tends to show up as flat or falling margin well before it shows up anywhere else in the reporting.

The practices handling this well are not slowing down their use of AI. They are repricing around the scope and outcome delivered rather than the time it took, and tracking margin per engagement rather than relying on utilisation alone to tell the full story.

If that pattern sounds familiar, it is worth a proper look before a quiet quarter forces the conversation. Read the full piece on the blog for how the gap forms and what to measure instead.
